I grew up in a world that held both old-money and new-money types, and after decades of life I have a belief: there's a challenge with first-generation wealth when it comes to the character of their children, and obesity is one part of the outcome.

When someone moves up from a lower to a higher economic status, they typically grew up with some degree of adversity. There were challenges to overcome, hard work that was required of them, and other such things. These, in turn, build character, and that character typically lasts with the parents even after they have become successful and quite comfortable; they remember what got them where they are today, and know the value of it.

Their children, on the other hand, live a life with much less difficulty, and this can be a curse. When you look at old-money families, you notice that they have a tradition of imposing adversity upon their children in productive ways...making them earn an allowance, making them work summer jobs doing hard work in service to others, etc. This tradition is typically the key to inherited wealth surviving from generation to generation, in fact. I've known about half a dozen "trust-fund kids" without such an upbringing, and they have all seemed somewhat lost and adrift. They wanted to do something with their lives, but it was like the lack of challenges deprived them of any kind of focus.

But I digress. I would wager that in nearly every single case, the parents of the chubby kids were parents who grew up with far less money than they currently have. They haven't figured out how to temper their own children with adversity and challenges, and as a result the kids are lazy fat shits.
